headline: Aspiring Machine Learning Engineer · AI, Data Science & applied Python
bio:
I am NTARINDWA Jean Dieudonne, an aspiring Machine Learning Engineer based in Kigali. I focus on Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, and I use programming to turn models into usable tools.

I am pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Information Technology at Rwanda Polytechnic (RP) – Huye College, with expected completion in 2027. Alongside coursework I study machine learning in practice: classification and regression, data preprocessing, feature engineering, model training and evaluation, and the fundamentals of deep learning for image classification.

I also have more than one year of IT infrastructure and helpdesk experience, which taught me to work carefully with real systems and users. Python is my main language for ML work. JavaScript, Node.js, FastAPI, and React help me deploy and integrate models in web and mobile applications.

I am looking for junior and internship roles in machine learning, AI engineering, and data science, where I can keep learning while contributing to intelligent solutions for real problems.

education.description: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, expected in 2027. Studies include programming, databases, and information systems. Parallel self-study in machine learning, data science, and application development.

experience.title: IT Intern
experience.description: Support IT infrastructure and respond to end-user technical requests within a leading industrial group. Configure network settings and manage Active Directory profiles to support consistent user access across manufacturing and logistics. Maintain Office 365 environments, troubleshoot hardware and software issues, and resolve tickets in collaboration with the senior IT team.

experience.title: IT Intern
experience.description: Troubleshot hardware and software issues for diverse end users and provided practical technical support. Maintained network configurations and performed routine system maintenance, using PowerShell to automate basic administrative tasks. Resolved user-access issues, managed IT equipment through ticket procedures, and applied cybersecurity fundamentals while supporting district data and helpdesk operations.

experience.title: Machine Learning & Software Projects
experience.description: Build applied ML and software projects: image classification with PyTorch and EfficientNet-B0, linear regression for student performance prediction, FastAPI services, React interfaces, and Android work with JavaScript. Use Python for modeling and JavaScript/Node.js to integrate models into applications people can use.

projects.title: Banana Leaf Disease Detection System
projects.summary: Image classification of banana leaf diseases with EfficientNet-B0, served through FastAPI and a React interface.
projects.description: Problem: farmers and agronomists need a practical way to distinguish common banana leaf conditions from photos. I developed an image classification workflow using EfficientNet-B0 in PyTorch for four classes: Cordana, Healthy, Pestalotiopsis, and Sigatoka. Work covered data preparation, model training and evaluation, then integration of the model behind a FastAPI backend and a React frontend so predictions can be used in an application. This project shows how I connect computer vision with deployable software. A public repository is not listed yet.

projects.title: Student Performance Prediction
projects.summary: Linear regression that relates study hours to examination scores, with correlation analysis and an interactive predictor.
projects.description: Problem: estimate how study time relates to exam performance using a simple, explainable model. I implemented linear regression, inspected the relationship between study hours and scores, and wrapped the model in an interactive prediction application so users can try different inputs. The public repository is work_linear_reguration on GitHub (JavaScript).

projects.title: Machine Learning practice notebooks
projects.summary: Hands-on notebooks for core machine learning concepts, data work, and model evaluation.
projects.description: A public GitHub repository used to practice machine learning: algorithms, preprocessing, and evaluation in Jupyter notebooks. It documents how I study ML alongside coursework rather than a single production system.

projects.title: Professional Portfolio Platform
projects.summary: This FastAPI and React portfolio: public profile, projects, analytics, and a generated CV.
projects.description: Full-stack application used to publish my ML-focused profile. Built with React, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL (Neon in production-style hosting). Includes JWT authentication, a public page, PDF CV generation, project showcases, and visit analytics. Demonstrates that I can ship the software around a model, not only the notebook.

projects.title: Android application (Android Studio)
projects.summary: Native Android application work in Java using Android Studio.
projects.description: Mobile application practice in Android Studio with Java: user interface, application structure, and device-oriented software development. Complements web and API work when an intelligent feature needs a mobile client.

posts.title: How I trained a banana leaf disease classifier
posts.summary: EfficientNet-B0, four leaf classes, and serving the model through FastAPI.
posts.body: I built an image classifier for banana leaf photos using EfficientNet-B0 in PyTorch. The four classes are Cordana, Healthy, Pestalotiopsis, and Sigatoka. The useful part was not only training: I wrapped the model in FastAPI and a React interface so a photo can return a prediction. That is the pattern I want to keep using — a notebook is a start, a hosted API is the product.

posts.title: Study hours and exam scores with linear regression
posts.summary: A small, explainable model and an interactive predictor.
posts.body: Linear regression is a good first model when the question is simple: how does study time relate to exam scores? I inspected that relationship, then put the model behind an interactive predictor so someone can try different hours and see an estimated score. Explainable models still matter when you are introducing machine learning to a real workflow.

posts.title: From Jupyter notebooks to a public ML profile
posts.summary: FastAPI, React, Neon Postgres, and a CV you can download.
posts.body: This site is the software around my machine learning work. The public profile, project cards, contact inbox, and PDF CV are all backed by FastAPI and PostgreSQL. The ML lab can talk to a Colab session when a model is loaded. I use it as a living resume: visitors can read the work, try a prediction, and write to me without creating an account.
